findings.reason: the first implementation node should extend these two reconcilers rather than author a parallel recovery rule, and citing them changes the node's file scope and its reuse story.
findings.text: the plan's §3 "recover origin from surviving generation evidence" rule already exists as `reconcile_catalog_edit_origins`, which re-derives `StandardName.origin` from surviving `StandardNameSource`/`PRODUCED_NAME` evidence (derived wins over dd/signals, else unset) for exactly the `catalog_edit` cohort the plan names, and §3's paired "status ... recovered in the same pass" already exists as `reconcile_catalog_status` at graph_ops.py:14266 (null `status` → `draft`); the plan cites neither, so an implementer would rebuild both

findings.reason: naming it forces the author to state which of the existing anchors the new evidence (LLMCost, DocsRevision, REFINED_FROM) slots into, instead of a parallel recoverer.
findings.text: the plan's recovery pass does not cite `rebuild_provenance`, the 187-line entry point (with `catalog_reconcile.reconcile_catalog` documented in-module at catalog_reconcile.py:1-18 as "the only path that rebuilds provenance from a published catalog"), which already carries a descending-authority recovery map (`load_recovery_map`, `DEFAULT_RECOVERY_REF = a2f8831`, scalar-anchor and change-history fallbacks) and an idempotent dry-run; the plan's "generation evidence, not import markers" decision is the same shape; it must say whether it extends this tree or starts a second

findings.reason: the honest change is to install the existing boundary on the live path, not to add a second guard, and the plan should name the boundary it installs.
findings.text: §4's guard is a thin policy layer over machinery that already refuses catalog payloads: `guard_catalog_write_payloads` → `protection.refuse_pipeline_authority_loss` at protection.py:183 refuses a whole batch that would clear or replace pipeline authority, and `record_catalog_import_provenance` at catalog_import.py:51 already reduces any caller payload to exactly `{id, catalog_commit_sha}` with `MATCH` (no `MERGE`) so `origin` and `status` are structurally unreachable; the plan does not say why these cannot be extended

findings.reason: a forked guard drifts from the shared owner (`origin` is currently absent from `PROTECTED_FIELDS` and `PIPELINE_AUTHORITY_FIELDS`, so the owner is the one place that needs the fix), and the plan's own §4 argument is prevention, which only holds if the live owner is guarded.
findings.text: §4 forks a guard whose owner is `catalog_import.record_catalog_import_provenance`; the census of the same mechanism across the tree is: catalog_import.py:51 (allow-list receipt writer), catalog_import.py:109 `guard_catalog_write_payloads` (catalog-shape adapter), protection.py:183 `refuse_pipeline_authority_loss` (shared owner; `PIPELINE_AUTHORITY_FIELDS`/`PIPELINE_AUTHORITY_RELATIONSHIPS`), catalog_reconcile.py:201 (the one installed call site), and tests/standard_names/test_import_write_authority.py:14 and tests/standard_names/test_pipeline_authority_guard.py:11 (existing guard tests); the plan should extend `refuse_pipeline_authority_loss`'s authority field set to cover `origin` where the catalog is the caller, rather than fork a parallel import guard

findings.reason: the author must reconcile the two rules (does a pipeline-generated null recover to `active` or `draft`?) before any node writes status, or recovery will fight the standing reconciler.
findings.text: §3's paired claim that "status, cleared by the same import and null on 978 identities, is recovered in the same pass" duplicates `reconcile_catalog_status`, which already sets every null `status` to `draft` (and handles superseded/exhausted); the plan proposes to recover status from generation evidence, which contradicts the existing owner's rule (approval is the sole writer of `active`; null is a draft), so a second status writer would disagree with the installed one

findings.reason: the section must account for the added refusal surface in its own text, either by naming the existing refusal it installs or by stating why a new one is required.
findings.text: §4 adds a refusal family ("A catalog round-trip ... [is] entitled to nothing else on the editorial axis") and names no existing refusal it retires, merges, or extends, nor why nothing can be, against a supplied `refusal_families` count of 0; the same refusal is already raised by `record_catalog_import_provenance`'s `ValueError` on an empty id and by `refuse_pipeline_authority_loss`'s `PipelineAuthorityError`

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the plan proposes no new module; the recovery rule it specifies fits the decision tree `provenance_rebuild.rebuild_provenance` already hides (descending anchor authority: recovery map → surviving scalar → change history), so nothing new spreads complexity over the same machinery.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §4 re-implements the origin/status write guard whose owner is `imas_codex/standard_names/catalog_import.py:51` (with `protection.py:183` as the shared guard and `catalog_reconcile.py:201` as the installed call site), and §3 re-implements origin/status recovery owned by `graph_ops.reconcile_catalog_edit_origins` and `graph_ops.reconcile_catalog_status`.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §4 adds a refusal condition ("import may not touch the editorial axis") without naming what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be, even though the same refusal already exists in code.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the design adds an origin/status recovery rule and an import write guard without citing the existing `reconcile_catalog_edit_origins`, `reconcile_catalog_status`, `rebuild_provenance`, or `refuse_pipeline_authority_loss` in imas_codex/standard_names/, all of which already do the named jobs.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §4 adds a guard over catalog writes and does not say why `catalog_import.record_catalog_import_provenance` (the existing allow-list boundary) or `protection.refuse_pipeline_authority_loss` cannot be extended to carry it.
